features.name: any_comment_concrete_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a concrete real-world example?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment offers a concrete real-world example (a specific real case, event, person, organization, statistic from a real situation, or actual personal/observed experience) as support for its counter-argument; return 0 if no comment does (including abstract logic, hypotheticals, or generic claims only). Do not count hypothetical or invented scenarios. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

h0: any_comment_concrete_example has no association with delta (view change) rates.
h1: Rows with any_comment_concrete_example = 1 have a higher view-change rate than rows with 0.
note: Operational assumption: the comparison group "relying solely on abstract logic" is approximated by the absence of any concrete real-world example (0); this includes rows with mixed or other non-example content, and "solely abstract" is not separately measured. Presence is binary at row level. Comments are unordered and may include text from after the outcome; the exclusion of outcome announcements is applied in the prompt. Association only, not causal.
